whoIsThisFor.heading: Who should take the Advanced Field Service AP exam?

personas.label: Field Service leaders
personas.description: You manage a large technician organization and want to validate your knowledge of scheduling policies and optimization.

personas.label: Field Service consultants and administrators
personas.description: You already configure Salesforce Field Service and want to demonstrate deeper skills in complex scheduling, crews, inventory, and mobile work.

personas.label: Field Service specialists
personas.description: You focus on service operations projects and want an advanced credential beyond the consultant-level exam.

examDifficulty.heading: How challenging is the Advanced Field Service AP exam?
examDifficulty.summary: The exam goes deeper into scheduling design and optimization than the consultant-level credential. Be ready to explain how policies, work rules, service objectives, and optimization options affect a schedule.
bullets: 46 scored questions in 75 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
73% to pass, which is 34 correct answers out of 46.
Scheduling detail: Review work rules, service objectives, policies, and optimization modes.
Complex service operations: Study crews, multi-day work, shifts, inventory, and mobile workflows.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Practice troubleshooting schedules in a Field Service org. For each unscheduled appointment, identify the applicable rule, resource constraint, or objective. Confirm current exam requirements in the official guide before registering.

examFormat.heading: Advanced Field Service AP exam format
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online. Questions focus on advanced scheduling and field operations.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Many questions describe a scheduling or service problem, such as excessive travel or a job that needs multiple technicians, and ask which configuration should change.
bestWayToPass: Separate constraints from preferences: Work rules filter out unavailable or unqualified resources; service objectives rank the remaining options.
Choose the optimization mode: Know when to optimize several days, repair today’s schedule, or improve one resource’s schedule.
Plan complex work: Review service crews, appointment dependencies, and multi-day scheduling.
Understand mobile operations: Study offline priming, technician updates, inventory, and the information available in the field.

certificationCard.description: This exam covers advanced Salesforce Field Service setup, including scheduling policies, optimization, complex appointments, crews, inventory, maintenance plans, and mobile work.

keyConcepts.h2: Advanced Field Service AP: core concepts

blocks.heading: Scheduling Policies and Optimization
blocks.body: A scheduling policy combines work rules and service objectives. Work rules define constraints, such as required skills, territory, or availability. Service objectives rank the resources that meet those constraints, for example by travel time or arrival window. Optimization can improve schedules across appointments. Global optimization can plan a broader set of upcoming appointments, in-day optimization can respond to changes during the day, and resource schedule optimization can improve an individual technician’s schedule. Choose the mode that matches the scope and timing of the problem.

blocks.heading: Work Orders, Work Types, and Appointments
blocks.body: A work order describes the service job. A work type can provide a reusable configuration such as duration, required skills, or whether an appointment is created. The service appointment is the scheduled visit. Dependencies can order multiple appointments, while multi-day work supports jobs that span several days. A service crew or multiple assigned resources can support work that requires more than one person.

blocks.heading: Assets and Maintenance Plans
blocks.body: Assets represent products installed at customer locations. A maintenance plan can generate work orders on a recurring schedule for one or more assets. Plan settings can control the generation horizon and grouping. Asset history helps teams review prior visits and parts used. Warranty and entitlement information can help determine which service is covered.

blocks.heading: Inventory and Parts
blocks.body: Locations can represent warehouses, depots, or technician vehicles. Product items track stock at a location. Product requests ask for parts, transfers move them between locations, and product consumed records parts used on a job. Where configuration supports it, required parts on a work type can help scheduling account for technician inventory.

blocks.heading: Mobile Work and Offline Access
blocks.body: The Field Service mobile app lets technicians review assignments, update work orders, capture signatures, and record time or parts. Offline work depends on downloading the required data to the device ahead of time, then syncing changes when connectivity returns. Administrators control what is primed. Mobile flows can add guided steps such as checklists, and status updates help dispatchers see current field progress.

scenarioTips.h2: How to prepare for the Advanced Field Service AP exam
scenarioTips.intro: First decide whether the issue is a hard scheduling constraint, a preference, a complex appointment, or a field execution need. Then select the configuration that owns it.

blocks.heading: Select an Optimization Scope
blocks.body: Use broad optimization for a set of upcoming appointments, in-day optimization to respond to changes today, and resource schedule optimization for one technician’s schedule.

blocks.heading: Model Complex Appointments
blocks.body: Use dependencies for work that must happen in sequence, multi-day scheduling for jobs spanning days, and crews or multiple resources for work requiring several people.

blocks.heading: Plan Resource Capacity
blocks.body: Capacity-based resources can be scheduled by a quantity such as hours or jobs within a period, rather than only by a specific appointment slot.

blocks.heading: Measure Field Service Results
blocks.body: Use measures such as first-time fix, travel time, utilization, and on-time arrival to understand service performance and scheduling outcomes.

blocks.heading: Configure the Mobile Experience
blocks.body: Choose offline data priming deliberately, use mobile flows for guided tasks, and keep technician status current for dispatchers.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Related credentials after Advanced Field Service AP
nextCertsAfter.intro: Continue with a Field Service, service operations, or Salesforce architecture credential.

sampleQuestions.question: A technician without the required certification keeps appearing in suggestions for electrical jobs. What should you change?
options: Add a service objective to prefer the account’s technician
Required work type skill and skill rule
sampleQuestions.explanation: Work Rules act as filters. A skill work rule removes technicians who do not have the required skill.
whyWrong: Job duration does not affect technician skills.
Objectives rank candidates but do not exclude them.
Turning off optimization does not filter out unqualified technicians.

sampleQuestions.question: The business wants to reduce driving time while still following all scheduling rules. What should be adjusted?
options: The serial numbers on the assets
sampleQuestions.explanation: Service Objectives rank schedule options. A higher weight for Minimize Travel tells the scheduler to prefer shorter trips.
whyWrong: The number of work types does not control travel time.
Page layouts do not affect scheduling.
Asset serial numbers do not affect travel time.

sampleQuestions.question: Several technicians called in sick, leaving gaps and conflicts in today’s schedule. Which optimization should you use?
options: Resource schedule optimization for one technician
No optimization; wait for the schedule to fix itself
Global optimization for the next two weeks
sampleQuestions.explanation: In-Day Optimization repairs today’s schedule after changes such as absences or emergencies.
whyWrong: Optimizing one technician will not fix the wider schedule.
Waiting does not fill the gaps or resolve conflicts.
Global optimization plans further ahead and often runs overnight.

sampleQuestions.question: A job requires two technicians to work together at the same time. How should you schedule it?
options: Create one appointment and expect two people to arrive
Schedule two appointments on different days
sampleQuestions.explanation: Service crews and multiple-resource scheduling let more than one person work on one appointment at the same time.
whyWrong: A longer job still has only one assigned person.
An appointment must be assigned to the needed resources.
Appointments on different days do not let the technicians work together.

sampleQuestions.question: Installing a pump must finish before an electrical connection job can start. How should you set this up?
options: Add a note to the description
sampleQuestions.explanation: Appointment dependencies tell the scheduler that one job must finish before another can start.
whyWrong: A note does not affect scheduling.
One long appointment cannot represent two jobs that need different skills.
Unrelated appointments may be scheduled in the wrong order.

sampleQuestions.question: A building’s lifts need an inspection every three months. How should the work orders be created?
options: Create each work order by hand every quarter
Create a Case for each inspection
sampleQuestions.explanation: Maintenance Plans create work orders on a schedule for the assets they cover.
whyWrong: Manual creation is easy to forget.
A report does not create work orders.
Cases track issues, and each inspection would still need to be created by hand.

sampleQuestions.question: A technician uses a spare part on a job. How should they record it so inventory stays accurate?
options: Record it as a Product Consumed item on the work order
Add the part to the work type’s required products
sampleQuestions.explanation: A Product Consumed record tracks the part used and reduces the stock at the technician’s location.
whyWrong: Deleting the product item removes its inventory records.
Required Products say what a job needs; they do not record what was used.
A Product Request asks for more stock; it does not record usage.

sampleQuestions.question: A technician’s van is low on a part. How should they request more?
options: Add the part as a required product on the work type
Record a Product Consumed item with a negative quantity
Transfer the part back to the warehouse
sampleQuestions.explanation: Technicians use Product Requests to ask for parts to be sent to their location.
whyWrong: Required Products say what a job needs; they do not order stock.
Product Consumed records parts used, not parts needed.
A transfer moves stock that has already been approved. Request the stock first.

sampleQuestions.question: Technicians often work in basements without a signal. What should be set up so the mobile app can still work?
options: Offline data priming for the records they need
Move the jobs to a different service territory
Create a mobile flow that saves data to a custom object
sampleQuestions.explanation: The app downloads needed records before a technician goes offline, then syncs changes after the connection returns.
whyWrong: Changing a territory does not put data on the device.
A flow still needs the required data on the device, so prime the data first.
Appointment duration does not affect connectivity.

sampleQuestions.question: Technicians must complete a safety checklist in the mobile app before each job. What should you add?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Mobile Flows guide users through steps such as a checklist in the mobile app.
whyWrong: Dashboards show data; they do not guide job steps.
Scheduling policies choose technicians; they do not provide checklist steps.
Service territories group work by area; they do not provide task steps.

sampleQuestions.question: A contractor should receive up to 40 hours of work each week, without fixed appointment times. How should they be set up?
options: As a regular resource with a fixed shift
sampleQuestions.explanation: Capacity-based resources are scheduled by hours or job count within a period, which suits this contractor arrangement.
whyWrong: A location is a place, not a person or contractor.
Regular resources are scheduled into specific time slots.
Assets are equipment at customer sites.

sampleQuestions.question: A scheduling policy includes Work Rules and Service Objectives. How do they differ?
options: Objectives remove candidates, then Work Rules rank those left
Both apply only to mobile users
sampleQuestions.explanation: Work Rules are pass-or-fail filters. Service Objectives score the options that remain.
whyWrong: This reverses the roles of Work Rules and Objectives.
Both can apply to scheduling, not only to mobile users.
They have different roles in a scheduling policy.

sampleQuestions.question: Customers keep booking appointment slots that technicians cannot reach in time. What should you check?
options: Travel time settings, such as street-level routing
sampleQuestions.explanation: Accurate travel times depend on routing settings and territories. Poor travel estimates can lead to impossible appointment slots.
whyWrong: Priority changes the order of work, not travel time.
Changing slot length does not correct inaccurate travel estimates.
Preferring a technician does not make travel estimates more accurate.

sampleQuestions.question: A new hire should get only simple jobs during their first month. How can you do this?
options: Do not assign them to a territory
Put them in a separate org
sampleQuestions.explanation: Skills and skill levels help the scheduler match each technician only to suitable jobs.
whyWrong: Without a territory, the technician will not get jobs.
A disabled user cannot do any work.
A separate org would cut the hire off from the rest of the team.

sampleQuestions.question: A manager wants to know how often technicians solve an issue on the first visit. Which measure should they use?
sampleQuestions.explanation: First-time fix rate shows how often a job is completed without a return visit. It is a key measure of service quality.
whyWrong: Travel time measures driving, not whether the issue was fixed.
On-time arrival measures punctuality, not whether another visit was needed.
Utilization shows how busy technicians are, not whether they fixed the issue on the first visit.
